Article Title: CM Omar Abdullah opens first J&K film fest, seeks to reclaim Kashmir's place in Indian cinema
Article Text:
Omar opens first J&K film fest, seeks to reclaim Kashmir’s place in Indian cinema

SRINAGAR: CM Omar Abdullah inaugurated the maiden edition of the International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK) on Monday evening, calling it a new chapter in the region’s enduring relationship with cinema. Reminding filmmakers across the country that Kashmir had long been a destination for cinema, much before Switzerland and other international locations became popular, Omar said, “We would like that trend to start again.”Filmmaker Vidhu Vinod Chopra , who grew up and studied in Srinagar, said IFFJK was an emotional homecoming for him. He urged young and aspiring Kashmiri filmmakers to “show the world what you can do”. For actor Fatima Sana Shaikh, whose mother is from Kashmir, returning to the Valley after many years has brought back childhood memories.Filmmakers from 30 countries are participating in the four-day (Sept 7-10) event, with more than 130 movies being showcased. The IFFJK has brought together an eminent jury comprising Santosh Sivan, Dorothee Wenner, Keiko Bang and Himansu Sekhar Khatua.

Article Title: 'I was disrespected and undermined': Former Pakistan coach drops bombshell, names 'untouchable' figure behind England tour mess
Article Text:
Aaqib Javed, Jason Gillespie

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan head coach Jason Gillespie has doubled down on his criticism of Pakistan chief selector Aaqib Javed , saying the selection committee chairman took control of Pakistan cricket and changed the direction the team was supposed to follow.Gillespie, who was appointed Pakistan's head coach in April 2024 and resigned in December that year, said he was brought in with a clear vision of rebuilding Pakistan's fast-bowling culture. According to him, that plan changed after Javed became the chief selector.“When I came on board, they wanted to bring back fast bowling,” Gillespie said, while talking to UK-based outlet The Telegraph. “This is what was sold to me when I took on the role. They wanted to prepare surfaces that would bounce and carry and would encourage fast bowling because they felt that fast bowling was dying. I was on board and thought: ‘This is going to be really cool.’"“The appointment of Javed fundamentally altered the landscape,” he adds. “From that moment, my relationship with Pakistan cricket completely changed. Aaqib came in and took over. It appeared to me that he was in charge of absolutely everything."Gillespie's comments come after Pakistan made drastic changes during their ongoing tour of England. Following defeats in the first two Tests at Headingley and Lord's, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) sent seven players home, removed Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul, and appointed Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke for the third and final Test in Birmingham starting September 9.There have also been reports that the PCB confiscated the phones of some players in England as part of an inquiry into the team's "discipline and conduct" during the tour.Senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha were among the players sent back to Pakistan before Hesson joined the squad. Fast bowler Khurram Shahzad and spinner Ali Usman, who featured in both Tests, were also released, while all-rounder Aamir Jamal and batter Mohammad Awais returned home without playing a match.Meanwhile, Gillespie said working under Javed left him feeling sidelined and disrespected.“I was totally disrespected and undermined and I direct that towards Aaqib Javed. At our first meeting he came in with bravado, bluff, and bluster, wanting to show he was the man in charge. He said: ‘This is what we need to do.’ I listened and said OK. But this kept on happening and I pushed back on a couple of his comments. I just felt from that moment on that it wasn’t going to work because he’d already decided what he was going to do. There was going to be no collaboration whatsoever," Gillespie added.The former Australia fast bowler said Javed had the backing of the PCB chairman and the board, which made him feel untouchable.“Aaqib had the support of the chairman and the board and that’s why he felt he was untouchable,” Gillespie says. “As a coach, you feel compromised. He was not a collaborative chairman of selectors. He doesn’t take on other people’s ideas, thoughts, or opinions. He might think he does, but he doesn’t. It was his way or the highway."Gillespie also claimed the PCB still owes him money from his time as coach but said he was not willing to change his principles to stay in the job.“The PCB still owes me thousands of dollars, but I was never going to be a yes man,” he says. “I wasn’t going to compromise on my principles, I never have throughout my career and I certainly wasn’t going to change.I could have stayed quiet, agreed to everything and taken home my salary, but that’s not me and part of me knew I was probably going to be sacked in a couple of months anyway.”Gillespie said Pakistan cricket remains trapped in a damaging cycle and lays the blame at the feet of Javed.“It’s heartbreaking for me to see what’s going on now, it’s a mess,” Gillespie said, as quoted by Telegraph. “I know the crux of it. It’s Aaqib Javed. He is the problem and as long as he is there, then Pakistan cricket will continue to go backwards," the former Pakistan coach said.
Article Summary: Former pakistan head coach jason gillespie has doubled down on his criticism of pakistan chief selector aaqib javed. Gillespie said he was brought in with a clear vision of rebuilding pakistan's fast-bowling culture. According to him, that plan changed after javed became the chief selector.

Article Title: Alex Eala could face heavy WTA punishment after choosing Philippines at Asian Games over China Open
Article Text:
Alex Eala reveals surprising dating red flags before US Open as she opens up about what instantly turns her off

Eala chooses Asian Games over China Open

Alexandra Eala (AP Photo)

PHILTA asks WTA to protect Eala from punishment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Alex Eala could face a fine and ranking consequences after choosing to represent the Philippines at the Asian Games instead of competing at the China Open, although her federation has formally asked the WTA to grant her an exemption.The decision comes after Eala's impressive run at the 2026 US Open, where she reached the third round before losing to American teenager Iva Jovic at Arthur Ashe Stadium. She has now confirmed that her next tournament will be the Singapore Tennis Open, before she heads to Japan to represent the Philippines at the Asian Games.Eala explained after her US Open defeat that the opportunity to compete for her country was too important to pass up.Speaking to the media after her loss to Jovic, Eala confirmed that she expects to play in Singapore before joining the Philippine team at the Asian Games.“Yes, before (Asian Games) I believe, I will be in Singapore,” Eala said, via Tennis Head.“But yeah, I love playing and competing with the Philippines team and in the SEA, the Asian Games I've also done, I think it's a really fun environment, I love being with the team.”Eala added: “Especially this last SEA Games in December, I had such a great time and I think they're really memories that will stick with me.“You know, the Asian Games happens once every four years and yeah, I just found myself drawn to compete in that over other stuff.”That commitment means Eala will miss the 2026 China Open in Beijing, which is scheduled to take place later this month at around the same time as the Asian Games.According to the Daily Tribune , Eala is one of only two players inside the women's top 20 rankings who will miss the China Open, with world No.15 Victoria Mboko currently sidelined by injury.Eala's decision could therefore leave her facing potential punishment from the WTA.According to Tennis365 , the China Open is a WTA 1000 event, making it one of the tournaments regarded as mandatory for players ranked high enough to qualify. The WTA's rules allow players to miss mandatory events in certain circumstances, including injury, other medical issues and personal reasons.Players who miss such an event without an applicable exemption can receive zero ranking points for the tournament. The effect on Eala's ranking, however, would depend partly on how other players perform at the US Open and Singapore Open.She could also face a $10,000 fine, according to the WTA's 2026 rulebook. That is the reported late-withdrawal fine for players ranked between 11th and 25th.Whether the Asian Games will qualify Eala for an exemption remains unclear.The Philippine Tennis Association (PHILTA) has already formally approached the WTA over the matter, requesting that Eala be exempted from the penalties because she will be representing her country.PHILTA secretary-general John Tiangco, who is also the mayor of Navotas City, confirmed the request to GMA Network. “We have formally informed the WTA that Alex will be representing the Philippines at the Asian Games and have requested an exemption so she will not be penalized for missing a WTA 1000 event,” Tiangco said.“Alex herself has made it clear that representing the Philippines is an honor and that she is choosing to play for the flag,” he added.“We fully support that decision and are doing everything we can to ensure that choosing to represent her country does not come at the expense of her standing on the WTA Tour.”Eala has plenty of experience representing the Philippines on the international stage. She is a two-time Asian Games bronze medallist, having finished third in both the women's singles and mixed doubles, and she won gold in the women's singles at the 2025 Southeast Asian Games in Thailand.Her decision comes during the best period of her professional career so far.Eala won her first WTA singles title in Washington D.C. in August and has climbed to a career-high No.18 in the world rankings. Her run at the US Open was also her best finish at the tournament, with her campaign ending against Jovic in the third round.Her rapid rise has made Eala one of the biggest emerging names in women's tennis, with her US Open appearance even contributing to a significant surge in ticket prices as fans rushed to watch the Filipina compete on one of the sport's biggest stages.The China Open would have offered another major opportunity, with the WTA 1000 event carrying valuable ranking points and bringing together many of the world's leading players.Instead, Eala has chosen the Asian Games.The decision now rests with the WTA, which will determine whether her commitment to representing the Philippines provides sufficient grounds for an exemption from the penalties associated with missing the mandatory Beijing tournament.
Article Summary: Alex eala could face a fine and ranking consequences after choosing to represent the philippines at the asian games instead of competing at the china open. The decision comes after eala's impressive run at the 2026 us open, where she reached the third round before losing to american teenager iva jovic.

Article Title: Duleep Trophy final: Ishan Kishan signals red-ball intent with mammoth 270
Article Text:
East Zone's captain Ishan Kishan plays a shot on day 2 of the Duleep Trophy 2026-27 final cricket match between South Zone and East Zone, in Chennai. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: Ishan Kishan has developed a habit of saving his best for the big occasion. Last year, he led Jharkhand to the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy title and produced a match-winning century in the final, a performance that helped him earn his way back into India's T20I setup. After playing a matchwinning hand against Pakistan in Colombo in the T20 World Cup earlier in the year, Kishan delivered again in the Duleep final on Monday, leading East Zone against South at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.Kishan smashed 270 off 334 balls (30x4, 7x6), taking East to a mammoth 708 all out, Kumar Kushagra chipping in with 101 as well. The double century, his second in first-class cricket, came after a gap of 10 years and has further strengthened his case for a return to India's red-ball setup.A triple century seemed on the cards after he crossed 250, but Kishan said that personal landmarks never occupied his mind. Interestingly, he himself was unaware that it had been 10 years since he scored a first-class double century. "Honestly, I wasn't even thinking about 50, forget 300. I was only thinking about 50-run partnerships," Kishan said.The double century came off 273 balls. He then accelerated dramatically, reaching 250 in only 27 more balls.But the intent, he said, was never to chase numbers. "I didn't change anything in my game plan. I was just batting normally. Once I got set, my thought was not to throw my wicket away. I have enough confidence in my shots to know that if I play well, I will either clear the field or find the gap," he said.For Kishan, the most satisfying aspect of the innings was the temperament he showed. With East having won the toss and opted to bat, the priority was to build a total that would put South under pressure. "I would rate this innings very highly because I kept the team's goal ahead of my own runs. There were moments when I could have played more attacking shots, but the priority was to spend time in the middle, make good decisions and build a big total," he said.That approach was shaped by a mindset Kishan believes has changed considerably during his time away from the Indian team. Having spent to two years grinding it out in domestic cricket, he said the experience taught him to simplify his game. "When you're playing for India regularly, sometimes you get into a flow and your growth can stagnate. Going back to domestic cricket makes you start from zero. You realise there are so many players scoring runs and that you have to perform better to get back," he said.
Article Summary: East zone captain ishan kishan scores a double century in duleep trophy final. The 270 came off 334 balls and was his second in first-class cricket in 10 years. He led east to a mammoth 708 all out, with kumar kushagra chipping in with 101.

Article Title: Carlos Alcaraz gets into groove, beats local favourite Tommy Paul to reach US Open quarterfinals
Article Text:
Carlos Alcaraz

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW YORK CITY: There was a moment early in the US Open fourth-round match when Tommy Paul was pulled wide, he lunged forward and, out of nowhere, slammed a forehand winner around the post, landing it behind a stunned Carlos Alcaraz. The crowd gasped, and a flicker of a smile crossed Paul's face. That was the kind of tennis the 29-year-old needed to produce just to make the match competitive against the defending champion.Instead, it was Alcaraz's forehand that lit up Arthur Ashe. The Spaniard ripped it from just about anywhere on the court, threading the needle and neutralising the American's serve as much through positioning as timing. The second seed finished with 33 winners, 17 of them off the forehand side.The world No. 3, returning from a four-month injury-enforced break, advanced to the quarter-finals with a statement 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 win, having dropped just one set across four matches.Sunday was the pair's ninth meeting, with Alcaraz now leading the head-to-head 7-2. Paul, the world No. 21, had won two of their first three meetings back in 2022-23, but on Sunday he admitted he was nowhere near the level required."It sucks! It felt like he's playing at a completely different level than me.It sucks, because you feel like, sh@#t!" Paul said. "But at the same time, you learn a lot every time you play him. Every time I've played him, we've gone to the practice court with new ideas of what he does well and what I can try and put into my game."The practice court had also played a part in Alcaraz's own turnaround in the first week.After his third-round win over China's Yibing Wu, in which he had managed just nine winners off his forehand while making 19 unforced errors on the same side, the Spaniard went back to work."For a tennis player, it's really important how you go to bed in terms of feeling. Especially when you win the match, but you don't feel like you've been hitting the ball well, it is better to go back to the practice court and then just hit for five-ten minutes. Just to hit some balls when you're not nervous or you're not thinking about anything else. Leave the site with a good feeling."Alcaraz left Flushing Meadows feeling a lot better about his forehand on Friday."I think everybody saw the difference in my forehand today," he said.The 23-year-old, who exchanged his espresso-brown gear for a black-and-white look, also noted that his Grand Slam off-days now look very different from previous years.Golf had been his favourite escape when he wanted to get away from the pressure of the tennis court. But after the wrist injury, he cannot risk putting his wrist through the demands of the game. These days, his downtime is about recovery and preparing for the next round.Alcaraz will play the eighth-seeded American Ben Shelton next in the last-eight on Tuesday. The 23-year-old moved past Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 and is into his sixth major quarter-final and his second at Flushing Meadows, where he made the semi-finals in 2023.Meanwhile, Frances Tiafoe shocked 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (1), 6-4, 7-6 (6) to earn one of his biggest wins of the season.The 28-year-old world No. 12, roared on by the home crowd, was pumped up for his clash on Louis Armstrong Stadium as he reached the quarter-finals in New York for the fourth time.The two-time US Open semifinalist had lost six of his previous seven meetings with Medvedev, but was the sharper and more focused of the two through the two-hour, 57-minute contest. Tiafoe will face compatriot Alex Michelsen in the last-eight.
Article Summary: Carlos alcaraz beats tommy paul to reach us open quarter-finals. World no. 3 returns from four-month injury-enforced break. Frances tiafoe stuns 2021 champion daniil medvedev to reach last eight.

Article Title: Jasprit Bumrah will hold key to NZ series, says Mitchell Santner
Article Text:
Jasprit Bumrah

How crucial will it be for India to adapt to conditions given only a few players from the current set-up have played Tests in NZ?

What's your take on India's pace attack?

Did you have a look at Manav Suthar?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What do you think about India's struggles in Test cricket recently?

How important is ETPL for the European players, who don't always get to play a lot of top-quality cricket?

CHENNAI: The road to the World Test Championship (WTC) final for India is getting tougher, with every series carrying greater significance. The task has become even more challenging after they failed to win the final Test against Sri Lanka recently.India's next step takes them to New Zealand for a two-Test series, having not won there in a decade and a half. NZ's premier left-arm spinner Mitchell Santner , who is leading Edinburgh Castle Rockers in the ongoing European T20 Premier League (ETPL), told TOI in an exclusive chat that India's pace attack, led by Jasprit Bumrah , will play a major role in the final outcome of the series. Excerpts...The first thing is to try and understand the conditions as quickly as possible. A few players have been there before and done well. In Oct-Nov, the pitches can play differently compared to Feb-March. So, early in the season in New Zealand, the ball might move around a little bit. It is about getting your head around that.Bumrah leading the attack and being able to nip and swing the ball will hold the key. (Mohammed) Siraj has done it for a long time as well and (Prasidh) Krishna is obviously bowling well.There is a lot of variety, which is what you need.He has been very impressive since he made his debut. He gets nice and tight to the stumps and gets good shape on the ball. He does bowl with good overspin when he needs to and that is the key in NZ, trying to get a bit of bounce especially if there is grass. I think there is still a role for a spinner in NZ, especially in Tests alongside the quicks, whether it is first or second innings when the pitch might be holding up.On days four and five, it could spin a bit. Whether it is Jadeja or Suthar, both are very good options.I think it has always been a challenge. They always play the best teams, and then having to adapt to the conditions quickly is the main thing. But they have got all bases covered.It is perfect for Scottish, Irish and players from Holland. It gives them more exposure and opportunity to play against some good players. We have seen how good they are in their own right. To be fair, in the last few years, we have had some great games against Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands. You throw a few overseas players in, and the tournament (ETPL) is really strong.There is some great cricket on show already, which is good. And we are only halfway through.
Article Summary: India's next step takes them to new zealand for a two-test series. Nz's premier left-arm spinner mitchell santner says india's pace attack will play a major role in the final outcome of the series. Santner is leading edinburgh castle rockers in the ongoing european t20 premier league.

Article Title: Picking Bumrah for Asian Games is a good idea: Sunil Gavaskar
Article Text:
Jasprit Bumrah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'Asian Games title defence won't be easy'

(This interaction was facilitated by Sony Sports Network)

Bengaluru: The BCCI's decision to send a full-strength squad to the Asian Games later this month has brought one name into focus - Jasprit Bumrah. The premier India pacer has not played for India since the second ODI against England in Cardiff in July, when he limped off after suffering an impact injury to his left knee. He has since been undergoing rehabilitation and is part of India's squad for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan, although his participation is subject to fitness clearance.With the Asian Games in Japan beginning later this month, former India captain Sunil Gavaskar believes the tournament could provide Bumrah with valuable game time ahead of India's next major assignment, the New Zealand tour.The Asian Games, then, is the perfect opportunity for Bumrah to ease back into competitive cricket before that series. "There's a fair gap between the Asian Games and the New Zealand series, so playing Bumrah in the Asian Games is actually a good idea because he has to get some bowling under his belt. In Sri Lanka, we heard Mohammad Siraj was not quite in rhythm because he hadn't played enough in competitive matches. The bowlers need to get some overs and Bumrah getting them is very essential," Gavaskar said.Although Shreyas Iyer has lost six of the seven T20Is he has led India in this year, Sunil Gavaskar backed him. "He's very experienced as a captain, having led Kolkata Knight Riders, Delhi Capitals and Punjab Kings. I don't think there should be any pressure on him at the Asian Games. "Gavaskar was quick to add that the title defence won't be an easy ride for India. "It's going to be tough because it's a T20 tournament. Bangladesh are in form, Pakistan are always dangerous and Sri Lanka are a terrific team, not to forget Afghanistan, so it's not going to be easy at all," he said. Gavaskar pointed out that the Asian Games will be a huge learning experience for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. "To be able to meet sportspersons from other sports from across Asia can be an absolute treat. For Sooryavanshi, I hope it turns out to be even more inspirational because he will get to rub shoulders with athletes who he's looked up to."
Article Summary: Jasprit bumrah is part of india's squad for the three-match t20i series against afghanistan. The premier india pacer has not played for india since the second odi against england in cardiff in july, when he limped off after suffering an impact injury to his left knee.

Article Title: ‘We’ll sacrifice points’: World No.1 Sabalenka fires warning at WTA, ATP to end mandatory events over brutal schedule
Article Text:
Aryna Sabalenka, of Belarus, reacts as she competes against Taylor Townsend, of the United States, during the fourth round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)

Sabalenka wants players to choose what is best for their health

Sabalenka could sacrifice ranking position despite No.1 milestone

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Aryna Sabalenka has called on the WTA and ATP to scrap mandatory tournaments altogether, warning that players may have to sacrifice ranking points and positions if the increasingly demanding tennis calendar is not eased.The world No.1 joined Carlos Alcaraz in speaking out about the workload during the US Open, with the Spaniard revealing that he intends to start taking longer breaks and skipping tournaments rather than attempting to play every required event.Sabalenka went a step further, arguing that players should have greater control over their schedules so they can protect their bodies.The tennis calendar has become an increasingly contentious issue in recent years, with players facing mandatory commitments at WTA 1000 level as well as requirements to compete in WTA 500 events depending on their ranking and eligibility.There are 10 WTA 1000 tournaments on the 2026 calendar, several of which have been expanded to 12-day formats, adding to the number of weeks elite players are required to spend competing at the highest level.Missing mandatory tournaments can also carry financial and ranking-point consequences, making it harder for players to simply take time away from competition when they feel they need to recover.Alcaraz raised the issue after reaching the third round of the US Open, saying he wants to take more time away from the sport rather than allow the schedule to dictate his entire season.“I want to have the breaks that I need to prepare the tournaments, to have the time to prepare the tournaments, to miss the tennis, to miss the tour, to miss you guys,” Alcaraz said.“I think that’s really important.”The Spaniard, who was competing at his first tournament in four and a half months at the US Open, also made clear that he expects to miss more tournaments in the future.“In the future, I’m going to take some breaks, some long breaks,” Alcaraz said.“Maybe not four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it’s impossible to play them all.”Sabalenka backed the sentiment but believes the solution should go further than simply allowing individual players to skip the occasional event.“I would love to see changes to the calendar and eliminate the mandatory events to let the players decide what's best for their health,” Sabalenka said.She acknowledged how difficult it is to maintain the intensity required at the top of the sport across such a long season.“It’s been incredibly intense. Especially if you play at the level Carlos plays, which is basically very consistent, it’s very hard on the body.”Sabalenka then issued a warning about what could happen if the tours refuse to reduce the demands.“If they’re not going to reduce it, we’ll have to sacrifice points, ranking position, whatever it takes, to protect our bodies,” she said.“I think it would be really helpful for the WTA and ATP to relax the calendar a bit for us in order to truly support our health.”The current structure requires top-ranked players to compete at the mandatory WTA 1000 events, while players can also have obligations at the WTA 500 level. On the men's side, Alcaraz faces a similarly packed schedule involving the mandatory Masters events and selected 500 tournaments.Sabalenka's comments come as she approaches a significant milestone at the top of the women's rankings.She has spent 99 consecutive weeks as world No.1, but reaching 100 weeks is not guaranteed.The Belarusian must successfully defend her US Open title to retain her position, while a strong run from Elena Rybakina could prevent her from extending her reign. Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff could also enter the race for the top ranking, depending on how far they progress at the final Grand Slam of the season.Despite the significance of the milestone, Sabalenka said she is trying not to become consumed by rankings projections or outside speculation.“I completely separate myself from that because it's just like guessing,” she said.“I'm just trying to bring my best tennis every time I'm competing out there and basically fight for it.”She added that social media constantly produces new statistics and predictions, but she prefers to stay away from them.“There's always different statistics that social media brings. So I'm just completely away trying to stay away from it.”For Sabalenka, the same principle applies to the possibility of losing the No.1 ranking.“The situation is under my control for now, so I'm just trying to control what I can,” she said.“When it's no longer in my hands, it will no longer be in my hands. Why would I even think about it?”

Article Title: 'That was a pity': Viswanathan Anand after losing on time to Magnus Carlsen, who lauds India's 'love for chess'
Article Text:

GCL 2026 : Schedule for Day 4, Tuesday, September 8

BENGALURU: The fast-paced world of chess has seen many terms evolve over time. “Flagging” is one of them. It generally refers to winning a game purely on time when an opponent’s clock hits 0:00, regardless of the evaluation on the board. From the perspective of both players and spectators, it’s a tense, chaotic climax where speed outruns strategy.On Monday, that exact high-wire drama took centre stage during the Day 3 marquee clash between APL Pipers' Magnus Carlsen and Alaskan Knights' Viswanathan Anand on the icon board. With seconds ticking down in a sharp middle-game battle, Anand failed to hit his clock in time, allowing Carlsen to snatch a win on time."A few moves ago, I had a few seconds more than him, so somehow my brain stopped looking at the clock, and I didn't keep one second left,” Anand told reporters after the opening match of the day. "Once I make a move, I will get some time, but apparently I let my clock run out. That was a pity, but I'm happy the team won."Despite losing his game, Anand’s squad pulled off the overall match victory. "I'm not happy with my play, but at least it didn't cost us," the five-time world champion added.The current World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen also gave his side of the dramatic finish against his longtime rival."I felt like I was playing him a little bit in the middle game.I was pretty happy with the position from the opening, and then again I was a little bit shaky with little time,” Carlsen stated.“For a period there, he was defending very, very well, not making it any worse, and then I just obviously resigned myself to a draw. Then I randomly glanced at his clock and saw that it was out. That's how it goes sometimes at times like this."Later, in Pipers’ game against the Gambits, Carlsen also raised eyebrows by uncorking 3...f6 against World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov, before holding him to a draw.Explaining the unexpected move, Carlsen added, "It (the idea) was originally from my coach. It was a misclick, and then he started looking at it. I kind of like the general idea of taking kind of a random move in the opening, and then with computer analysis, you can make pretty much anything work. The main idea is that after castles, a6, it's actually already not terrible."Despite his self-described "underwhelming" form, Carlsen expressed deep appreciation for the crowd in Bengaluru, saying, "It's very nice to play here. Chess in India is massive. That's great to see, and I definitely want to come here and experience the love people have for chess."Day 3 saw intense action across four team face-offs. Alaskan Knights edged past Alpine APL Pipers 9–7 in the first match of the day, but the Pipers stormed back later in with a commanding, one-sided 15–3 win over American Gambits. Meanwhile, Mumba Masters dominated Ganges Grandmasters 12–3, while Triveni Continental Kings secured an 11–6 victory, their first in the tournament, over Alaskan Knights in the final match of the day.Following the Day 3 results, APL Pipers hold top spot with 9 match points, closely followed by Mumba Masters, American Gambits, and Alaskan Knights tied at 6 points each. Ganges Grandmasters and Triveni Continental Kings round out the bottom of the table with 3 match points apiece.3.30 PM: Ganges Grandmasters vs Alaskan Knights5.00 PM: American Gambits vs Mumba Masters6.30 PM: Triveni Continental Kings vs APL Pipers8.00 PM: American Gambits vs Alaskan Knights

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El rubius was eliminated from mrbeast's $1 million challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. Article Title: California’s Paradise High lost its town to fire in 2018 and Lahainaluna endured the Lahaina fire in 2023; their football teams have now met in Hawaii for the first ‘Unity Bowl’
Article Text:
High school football brings Lahaina and Paradise, Calif., together in “Unity Bowl.”

A meeting years in the making

More than a football weekender

Football: a source of strength

A new tradition born from tragedy

Two football teams separated by thousands of miles recently met on a Hawaiian field with a story that went far beyond the scoreboard. Both schools hail from communities ravaged by devastating wildfires and their initial meeting was intended to be a celebration of survival, rebuilding and the connections made from shared loss. Three years after the Maui wildfire and nearly eight years after the Camp Fire that destroyed Paradise, Paradise High School in California headed to Maui for the inaugural Unity Bowl against Lahainaluna High School. Most of the players at Paradise High were in elementary school when the 2018 Camp Fire tore through Butte County. As reported by Maui Now, on Nov. 8, 2018, the Camp Fire in Paradise displaced more than 50,000 people, destroyed over 18,000 structures and killed 85 people, marking it as the deadliest wildfire in US history at the time. Five years later, on Aug. 8, 2023, a wildfire tore through Lahaina and destroyed more than 2,200 buildings, killing 102 people in the deadliest wildfire in U.S. history. The fire also decimated Paradise, and residents tried to pick up their lives after widespread destruction. Lahainaluna High students on Maui faced a similar disruption after the August 2023 wildfire destroyed Lahaina. Many of the current seniors at the school were freshmen when the fire happened and still live with its effects.In both communities, their high school football programs have been important sources of identity and pride in difficult times. The Unity Bowl unites those experiences in sport, giving players from both schools a chance to meet others who understand what it means to rebuild after catastrophe.The concept for the showdown began in 2024 when Paradise High administrators reached out to Lahainaluna about establishing a home-and-home series. The first game was played at Sue D. Cooley Stadium, with Lahainaluna as the host on September 5. The schools also are planning a return meet in Paradise in 2027. Paradise made it to Maui after fundraising efforts helped cover the cost of the long trip from Northern California. Contributors included NFL quarterback and Butte County native Aaron Rodgers, who donated $15,000 toward the trip.The teams’ visit was way beyond game day. Players, coaches and parents from both programs came together for a community event at the OUTRIGGER Kāʻanapali Beach Resort. The players also had a chance to experience local culture and spend time together off the field with a lūʻau put on with Maui chef Zach Sato. The gatherings were designed to join young people who have suffered eerily similar disruptions while growing up on different sides of the Pacific.Both programs have shown in the past how sport can bring communities back to a sense of normalcy. Paradise’s 2019 season started with 12 straight wins, its first season after the Camp Fire. Lahainaluna has been one of Maui’s dominant football programs for more than a decade and has won multiple state titles. The Lunas' impressive 46-game streak of Maui Interscholastic League wins ended in 2024 but the team bounced back to make the state playoff and Paradise entered the Unity Bowl this season at 1-1, Lahainaluna at 0-2. But the records matter less than the meaning attached to the meeting.For the Lahainaluna seniors, the game holds special personal significance. Some still live away from their homes, which have not yet been rebuilt after the Lahaina fire. Paradise’s players have also been displaced and rebuilt a community, but at a much younger age. Their common experiences create a rare opportunity for intergenerational and inter-geographic connections. The Unity Bowl is not just a first-time football matchup. Two communities finding common ground, letting their youngest generation turn painful memories into lasting friendships.Image Courtesy: Hawaiʻi DOE
Article Summary: High school football brings lahaina and paradise, calif. together in “unity bowl.” the first game was played at sue d. cooley stadium, with lahainaluna as the host on september 5. The unity bowl unites those experiences in sport, giving players a chance to meet others who understand what it means to rebuild after catastrophe.

Article Title: True Samaritans: Indian volunteers take up grim task of cleaning decomposed bodies in Kathmandu
Article Text:
Volunteers of Hemkunt Foundation cleaning floors of a morgue in Kathmandu. (PC: Hemkunt Foundation)

DEHRADUN:

As rescue agencies continue recovering bodies from flash flood-hit areas in Nepal and bringing them to Kathmandu mortuaries, a group of young Indian volunteers has taken up a task few are willing to do — cleaning decomposed bodies before they are handed over to families and authorities for the last rites. The group has helped clean more than 30 bodies till now.At least seven volunteers -- Harteerath Singh, Neha Singh, Jag Singh, Jaskaran Singh, Ravi Singh, Amitose Singh and Harry Singh -- of Hemkunt Foundation, a Gurgaon-based non-profit organisation, are carrying out the work at the morgue of Maharajgunj Medical Campus, Kathmandu.One of the volunteers, Neha Singh, told TOI Friday that she travelled from Mumbai to Kathmandu for the voluntary service after coming across a social media post by the foundation, requesting volunteers to join them in Nepal. “The next thing I did was to fly down to Kathmandu without expecting anything,” she said, adding that volunteers were not known to each other before reaching there; and were now working as a family in this ‘sewa’ (selfless service).They say that they are totally focused on the task, and even the terrible stench of bodies has failed to deter them. Neha said, “We are here for the respect of the departed souls and the bereaved families.We don’t seek any publicity in that.”Another member of the group, Harteerath Singh, elaborated on some of the challenges being faced by them. “Due to the acute stench, sometimes, it becomes unbearable for us to stand inside the morgue even for a minute,” he pointed out.“But this is the ultimate ‘sewa’. At times, we don’t even bother to wear masks or gloves. We cover our faces with one corner of the turban cloth and just go inside to clean the bodies and floors of the morgue -- something which even the local authorities may not be willing to do,” Singh said.“We also see the positive side of it. It is the biggest opportunity for us to serve humanity.”
Article Summary: At least seven volunteers of hemkunt foundation, a gurgaon-based non-profit organisation, are carrying out the work at the morgue of maharajgunj medical campus, kathmandu. They say that they are totally focused on the task, and even the terrible stench of bodies has failed to deter them.

Article Title: Meet Callum Smith: The 23-year-old armless racing driver who steers with his feet at 110mph, joins Team BRIT alongside quadruple amputee Harvey Phillips and targets a historic Le Mans debut
Article Text:
Callum Smith has joined Team BRIT alongside quadruple amputee Harvey Phillips. (Photo: SWNS)

From watching bike racing with his grandad to driving at more than 110mph

How Callum Smith steers a race car using his feet

Born without arms, Callum Smith has adapted to racing by steering with his feet and controlling the pedals himself. (Photo: SWNS)

'My feet are like my hands'

Nine-year-old Callum Smith cycles using his feet. (Photo: SWNS)

A bold email to Team BRIT started his racing journey

'There's a lot of eye-to-foot coordination'

Callum Smith is working towards his racing licence and a potential Le Mans debut. (Photo: SWNS)

Quadruple amputee Harvey Phillips also joins Team BRIT

Harvey Phillips, a quadruple amputee, steers Team BRIT's race car using a specially adapted 3D-printed aid. (Photo: SWNS)

Team BRIT has its sights set on the 24 Hours of Le Mans

Callum Smith has never let the absence of arms stand between him and his passion for motorsport. The 23-year-old from Nuneaton, Warwickshire, was born without arms but is now chasing an extraordinary dream, becoming the first armless racing driver to compete at the legendary 24 Hours of Le Mans.Smith, a finance assistant, has signed his first driver contract with Team BRIT, described as the world's only competitive racing team made up entirely of disabled drivers. He is currently training in the team's modified BMW 1 Series at Donington Park as he works towards obtaining his racing licence.Callum Smith's love for motorsport began when he was just two years old. He would watch bike racing with his grandfather, Michael Smith, who was a major influence on his early interest in racing.His first track day came in July 2025 at Donington Park, where he reached a top speed of 90mph around the iconic 2.5-mile circuit. By April this year, he had pushed his speed further, recording 100mph on Silverstone's 3.66-mile Grand Prix circuit while driving his own Audi A3.He has since taken the next step by getting behind the wheel of Team BRIT's specially modified BMW 1 Series, where he has already reached speeds of more than 110mph.Speaking to SWNS, Smith said he always believed he had what it took to become a racing driver."Once I started getting into driving, I always had that self belief that I had what it took to be a racing driver and knew that I could do it."He added that Team BRIT had given him the opportunity to demonstrate his ability and pursue a dream that once seemed difficult to imagine.Smith drives using a specially designed steering plate created by Jim Doran Hand Controls. The system allows him to control the car using his feet.His left foot is used to steer, while his right foot operates the accelerator and brake. Additional controls have also been adapted to allow him to operate other functions inside the vehicle."On top of the accelerator I have an indicator switch – I have a Lodgesons Bleeper System which gives me buttons for the horn, main beam, window wipers etc.," he explained.Describing the steering system, Smith said, "I steer with my left foot. It's a steering wheel in the footwell that operates the steering wheel."Smith was born without arms because of an unexplained bilateral upper-limb disability. However, he says he has never regarded his disability as something that should prevent him from doing the things he enjoys."My feet are like my hands," he said, explaining that he writes with his right foot, plays video games such as FIFA and Call of Duty using his feet, and even plays the guitar that way.He also eats independently using a regular knife and fork.His approach to everyday life has helped him adapt naturally to driving, although racing presents its own set of challenges.Smith's opportunity with Team BRIT began with an email in which he asked whether the team would be willing to help make his racing ambitions a reality."The racing started off with an email to Team BRIT expressing my interest in racing and I said if they were interested in making my dreams come true, I'd be forever grateful," he recalled.The team responded, and Smith went through tests with instructors before completing a skid test. From there, his journey towards becoming a competitive racing driver began.He is now working towards securing his full racing licence. One of the challenges he has to overcome is demonstrating that he can independently undo his harness and open the car door.While Smith is confident behind the wheel, he admits that adapting to a race car has been challenging."It's hard, there's a lot of eye to foot coordination," he said.One of the biggest surprises for him has been the physical demands of racing, particularly the weight and stiffness of the steering."The biggest surprise to me is how heavy the steering feels in a race car, everything is stiffer," he said.Despite that, Smith remains determined to continue."But I love it and I'm quite keen to get it sorted, I'm motivated to get it done," he said, adding: "Confidence I'm not short of, but it's going to be a lot of hard work."Smith is not the only new driver hoping to make history with Team BRIT. The team's latest driver line-up also includes 21-year-old quadruple amputee Harvey Phillips from Louth, Lincolnshire.Phillips lost parts of both legs, his right arm up to the elbow, as well as fingers and thumbs on his left hand after suffering meningitis when he was nine months old.He has developed his own way of controlling the car. A lever allows him to accelerate and brake, while a 3D-printed cup attached to his right arm helps him steer."To accelerate and brake I have a lever, I twist it down to accelerate and push it down towards the dash to brake," Phillips explained.He added, "I have a 3D printed cup to slot my right arm into to turn the steering wheel."For Phillips, the immediate goal is to become comfortable with the race car and establish a competitive race pace."Getting comfortable with the car and getting a race pace down are the main aims for me," he said.But the team's ambition extends far beyond individual racing licences and track days. Team BRIT ultimately wants to become the first team comprising entirely disabled drivers to compete in the 24 Hours of Le Mans, one of the world's most prestigious endurance races.Both Smith and Phillips are now seeking sponsors as they embark on a year-long training programme. For Smith in particular, the journey represents the chance to break new ground in motorsport, and prove that the absence of arms does not have to mean the end of a racing dream.
Article Summary: Callum smith has signed his first driver contract with team brit. The 23-year-old is the first armless racing driver to compete at the 24 hours of le mans. He drives using a specially designed steering plate created by jim doran hand controls. His left foot is used to steer, while his right foot operates the accelerator and brake.
